page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-4 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by Ampere Altra processors running at a sustained clock frequency of 3.0 GHz. This configuration provides 2 dedicated physical cores addressing 2 vCPUs without multithreading, along with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The provisioned instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for direct network routing.

The instance relies entirely on remote block storage, featuring no integrated local NVMe or SSD capacity. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. The ARM64 Neoverse-based architecture eliminates thread contention by allocating single-threaded dedicated execution cores, providing consistent runtime execution characteristics for predictable compute cycles.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, Ampere Altra processors offer cost-effective compute capacity through high energy efficiency and lean resource footprints. Because the 4.0 GB memory footprint is constrained relative to modern database or large caching layers, workloads requiring dense in-memory datasets will require alternative sizing profiles or supplemental memory allocation.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-4 is suited for microservices, lightweight web servers, edge proxies, CI/CD build workers targeting ARM64 targets, and containerized dev-test environments.

Utilizing single-threaded physical execution cores without hyperthreading, the server ensures deterministic processing devoid of thread contention. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-4 is best matched for ARM application development, continuous integration runners, containerized API services, lightweight web routing, and general low-footprint cloud workloads.
